== Original post ==

'''Alter is money'''
* '''Author:''' Brad "Admiral Twk" Reinhold
* '''Published:''' September 1, 2004
* '''Rating:''' 4.85
* '''Description:''' Here is the real deck I played on day 2. I made it in 20 minutes, so I forgot to put in the two alters right before day 2. Here is the corrected decklist :)

=== Strategy ===

Here is a word to the wise: If you have an issue with a deck, and you don't have a clue, send a dmail to ask the person about their deck. Gomez seems to have a chip on his shoulder about something, but as to what I have no idea. I have deleted his .5 star review as being asinine, and because he offered up no real reason as to why he reviewed a winning deck so low.

Note To Gomez: Before you review something of mine in the future, please dmail me ;) Also, consider throwing yourself into that Carbonite Chamber I'm sure your using :)

Note: The version I played had 2 more emperors (making it 10 in total) but no alters. My 2 losses with this deck were to Savrip. (yes greg, you had savrip out, though that didn't matter as much in our game) :)

Basically, you play the same against averybody: get emperor down to the throne room so you can sac and add destiny, then go off of them. Use tauntaun skull to place womp rat or emperor palpy OOP to add to your power.

Note: If you do not have 8-10 palpatine:

hehe. You can use no less than 2 palpatines in the deck, but you can use Thok and Thug or tech mo'r in place of palpy. If you do, you will probably want to do 2 things:

<nowiki/>-1) add in inserts

<nowiki/>-2) Invest in some personal defense classes, cause your friends are going to hate you :)

reason for no janus:

in a deck like this you have to either have 3 or none (I played 2 at worlds and never saw him). I don't like having that many low destiny characters in the deck, so he's not in the deck. Some may argue that he makes up for it by cycling your cards and setting up destiny. Frankly, this deck just doesn't care. It has enough cyclable destiny and enough good destiny that if you can track at all you should be ok.

If you are in a game against a ground deck , you should do fine, just add to power, add destiny, and stack cards. Go to kessel for the win (I know you only drain for 1, but your deploy is a little better, they must have 6 ability, and you will probably replace their kessel, saving you some force until you are ready to go to space).

Against WHAP, Profit or TIGIH (or anything else like that), remember: Rats are good. Bubo is good.

Against TRM, the game will hang on the space battle. Either try to get more destinies than they can cancel, or just use sando to get one unstoppable destiny.

Against HB or a space deck, just sit the executor with flagship(v) at a system and sense/alter anything they try to do, while you sit maul in ship in front of a rebel at another system. When maul is at this system with the rebel, see if you can get Much anger in him on that guy and just cloak. You lose two, but they lose 4. Period :). Also, if they have luke in space, they will be losing 3 a turn to Your Destiny.

This deck is insane beats on the ground. In one fight on day 2, lone vader got attacked by EPP Quigon and Corran Horn. At the time I was playing epp vader, but I missed the swing, so the point is still valid: He fights, hits vader. I play tauntaun skull to add 6 to my power. I lose a force to add a destiny. I draw a 5 and a 6, while he draws a 3 I think (I had cancelled his colo with Sando). So I was power 23 with just vader to his power 11. And he stacks a card. It doesn't matter if they kill off vader in this version, because Ability(v) just gets him back, tauntaun skull is a used 5, and first strike retrieves the card you lost for the Emperor's Power.

this is an advanced deck, but it is also a lot of fun to play with. This is what BHBM fighting was meant to do: SAC things, kill things, stack cards.

Have fun!

<nowiki/>--Brad Reinhold.
